headings.text: Which distribution path applies to you?

blocks.html:
Once your plugin builds and runs, distribution is mostly about signing and API/version matching — plus understanding which distribution path applies to you.

Package a release build

This produces a minified, ProGuarded, release-signed APK named ATAK-Plugin-<name>-<PLUGIN_VERSION>-<versionName>-<ATAK_VERSION>.apk. Before you share it:

  • Match the ATAK version. A plugin only loads into an ATAK whose API matches its plugin-api marker. State the target ATAK_VERSION (and variant, e.g. CIV) alongside the download, and rebuild for each ATAK version you support.
  • Sign consistently. Keep your release keystore safe and reuse it, so updates are recognized as the same app.
  • Honor third-party licenses. Check THIRDPARTY.md for any library you bundle and include the required notices.

Which distribution path applies to you?

  • Play Store users — sign through TAK.gov (this guide's scope). The ATAK-CIV build on Google Play only loads plugins signed by the TAK Product Center. Your own release key is not enough: submit your built plugin through TAK.gov's Third Party Pipeline to get it signed (and optionally listed on TAK.gov), then distribute the signed APK — GitHub releases, your own site, etc. — within the terms of the ATAK-CIV license and the licenses of anything you bundle. An APK signed only with your own key installs fine, but Play Store ATAK-CIV refuses to load it.
  • Developer builds — your own key is enough. The ATAK-CIV developer build from the SDK accepts plugins signed with any key, including this guide's debug/release keys. That covers development, testing, and closed groups that side-load the developer build — it is not a path to Play Store users.
  • Government / controlled plugins. Plugins that build against the Military SDK, expose military-controlled capability, or are intended for foreign release go through the official TAK Product Center pipeline — build requests, data-rights/export determination, and keying for distribution (including Foreign Military Sales). That process is governed by tak.gov policy, not this guide; see TAK.gov's "Our Process" and "Third Party Pipeline" pages.

Versioning

Bump PLUGIN_VERSION for your own releases, and remember to tick **versionCode** in **AndroidManifest.xml** whenever you change **plugin.xml** (the file itself notes this) so ATAK picks up the change.
